passage: Home log, Sunday. I let the star block fall through its slot, and Manjula said "Drop!" and grabbed the block to do the same. Manjula held it flat over the hole and let go, and it bounced off the lid and rolled away. "Oops. Again," Manjula muttered, fetched it, and started from the top, this time tilting it a little. I said nothing. Yamini, Manjula's mother

qa.q: What did Manjula say when grabbing the star block?
qa.a: Manjula said "Drop!" and grabbed the block.

qa.q: What was Manjula feeling after the block bounced off the lid?
qa.a: Manjula was a bit disappointed but not discouraged; the mumbled "Oops. Again" and starting from the top show a wish to keep going.

qa.q: What could Manjula try instead of copying the drop, and why?
qa.a: Manjula could turn the block until it matches the star-shaped slot before dropping it, because copying the motion without matching the shape leaves the block on top.

qa.q: How does Yamini see the copying?
qa.a: Yamini watches quietly and lets Manjula fix the mistake alone; Yamini seems to trust that Manjula can learn from the bounce.

grounding: A toddler copies the mother's drop of the star but holds the piece flat, sees it bounce off, and starts again from the top.

passage: Playroom note, Wednesday. Tarun jammed the square block against the round hole and pounded it with a flat palm over and over. The palm turned pink and tears began, but the block stayed on top. I sat down beside Tarun, held the square and the circle side by side, and said, "Different." Tarun stared, then sniffed and picked up the circle piece instead. Tomorrow I will set the shapes out one by one. Kalyani

qa.q: What did Tarun pound with a flat palm?
qa.a: Tarun pounded the square block against the round hole.

qa.q: What was Tarun feeling when the tears began?
qa.a: Tarun was frustrated and upset, because all the effort was getting nowhere.

qa.q: What different approach could Tarun try, and why?
qa.a: Tarun could look for the hole that has the same shape as the block, because pushing harder cannot change the shape of the piece.

qa.q: How does Kalyani see Tarun's pounding?
qa.a: Kalyani sees hard effort that is going nowhere, so Kalyani sits down and shows the two shapes side by side rather than telling Tarun to stop.

grounding: A toddler hammers a square block on a round hole with a palm, using force that does not change the block's shape.

subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
passage: Playgroup note, Tuesday. Sabina held out a block that had stuck halfway in its hole and looked up at Nirmala, Sabina's mother. Nirmala gave it a slight turn, and Sabina pushed it home, then clapped. Later Sabina brought the next block over in the same way. I told Nirmala that asking was a fine first step and a small turn is something Sabina might try alone. The playgroup helper

qa.q: What did Sabina do after the block stuck halfway in its hole?
qa.a: Sabina held out the block and looked up at Nirmala.

qa.q: What was Sabina feeling when clapping at the end?
qa.a: Sabina was pleased and proud, having pushed the block home after the slight turn. 😊

qa.q: What could Sabina try before handing over the block, and why?
qa.a: Sabina could give the block a small turn alone before handing it over, because the turn is what got it to fit.

qa.q: How does Nirmala see being handed the block?
qa.a: Nirmala is asked for one small turn and sees it succeed at once, so she is likely glad to help and pleased to see Sabina finish it.

grounding: A toddler hands a stuck block to the mother, who turns it slightly before the toddler pushes it in.

passage: After many failed tries Wanjiru dropped the star block, pushed the puzzle box away and crawled off across the floor. Liam, Wanjiru's father, watched from the doorway and said nothing. Soon Wanjiru was stacking cups on the rug, one on top of another, humming. Liam tucked the puzzle box back on its shelf. "Another day," he said quietly.

qa.q: What did Wanjiru do after dropping the star block?
qa.a: Wanjiru pushed the puzzle box away and crawled off.

qa.q: What was Wanjiru feeling when pushing the box away?
qa.a: Wanjiru was frustrated and tired of the puzzle, and the humming over the cups shows the mood eased once the task was left.

qa.q: What could Wanjiru try on another day, and why?
qa.a: Wanjiru could come back to the puzzle fresh and try one shape at a time, or ask Liam to sit with the box, because a rested mood makes trying easier.

qa.q: How does Liam see Wanjiru leaving the puzzle?
qa.a: Liam treats it as a rest, not a failure, so he puts the box on its shelf and says "Another day."

grounding: After many failed tries a toddler drops the block, pushes the box away and moves to stacking cups, leaving the task for another day.

passage:
"Sofa, Jahnavi? Go on," said Salma.
Jahnavi lay flat on the cushion, tummy down, and kicked. "Uh." Slid off.
"Try again."
A knee hooked up. "Uh!" It slipped.
"Ooh, roll?" Jahnavi rolled sideways. "Oof."
Back to the knee, and this time it went over the edge. "Up!"
"That knee did it," Salma laughed. "Again?"

qa.q: What was Jahnavi's first way of climbing?
qa.a: Jahnavi lay flat on the cushion, tummy down, and kicked.

qa.q: What was Jahnavi feeling when the knee finally went over the edge?
qa.a: Jahnavi was thrilled and proud, shown by the shout of "Up!" after the slips.

qa.q: What alternative could help Jahnavi if the knee keeps slipping, and why?
qa.a: Jahnavi could grip the cushion with both hands as the knee goes up, or ask Salma to steady the cushion, because a firmer hold helps the knee stay.

qa.q: How does Salma see Jahnavi's tries?
qa.a: Salma cheers and gives small hints like "Try again" and "roll?", so Salma seems happy to let Jahnavi experiment and notice which way works.

grounding: A toddler tries belly-first, a knee hook and a sideways roll on the sofa, and stays with the version that gets the knee over the edge.

passage:
"Watch, Rashmi," said Baljeet, Rashmi's big brother. "Turn round, sit, legs up!" He spun, sat and swung his legs onto the sofa.
"Turn... sit... legs," Rashmi said, and did the moves loosely, landing halfway across the cushion on the tummy.
"Almost! Closer than last time."
"Again," said Rashmi, sliding down. "Turn. Sit. Legs."

qa.q: What three steps did Baljeet show Rashmi?
qa.a: Baljeet showed turn round, sit, legs up.

qa.q: What was Rashmi feeling after landing halfway across the cushion?
qa.a: Rashmi was pleased and eager to try again, shown by the quick "Again" and repeating the steps aloud.

qa.q: What alternative could help Rashmi finish the climb, and why?
qa.a: Rashmi could sit down first with a bottom right at the edge before swinging the legs, because the swing needs a firm start, and Baljeet could hold the cushion.

qa.q: How does Baljeet see Rashmi's copying?
qa.a: Baljeet is proud and encouraging, calling it "Almost!" and noting it is closer than last time.

grounding: A toddler watches an older brother turn, sit and swing his legs up, then copies the sequence loosely and lands closer than before.

subtype: Approach: using the caregiver as a tool [Action]
passage: In the flat's living room Ayesha stopped facing the sofa, lifted both arms high and said "Up." Charu, Ayesha's father, put down the newspaper, scooped Ayesha under the arms and set the toddler on the seat. Ayesha wriggled into the corner with a soft "Ah," and picked up the cushion. No climbing was needed at all.

qa.q: What word did Ayesha say in front of the sofa?
qa.a: Ayesha said "Up."

qa.q: What was Ayesha feeling with both arms raised at the sofa?
qa.a: Ayesha was trusting and expectant, sure Charu would do the lifting, and content once seated.

qa.q: What could Ayesha try in place of asking, and why?
qa.a: Ayesha could try hooking a knee onto the cushion edge first, with Charu close, because trying helps the legs learn a skill that lifting does not teach.

qa.q: How might Charu see this way of getting onto the sofa?
qa.a: Charu finds it quick and easy to lift Ayesha, and probably enjoys being asked, but may want to give a chance to climb sometimes.

grounding: A toddler lifts both arms and says "up" and the father lifts the toddler onto the sofa, so no climbing is needed.

passage: Reena stood at the sofa. First she scrambled belly-first and slid off. Then she stopped. "Knee!" she said, remembering the one that worked, and swung a knee onto the cushion edge, then the other leg over. Charu, Reena's mother, counted quietly. By the next evening Reena started every climb with the knee, and each time she was quicker than before.

qa.q: How did Reena start every climb by the next evening?
qa.a: Reena started every climb with the knee on the cushion edge.

qa.q: What was Reena feeling when saying "Knee!"?
qa.a: Reena was confident and pleased, because she remembered a move that had worked and chose it. 🙂

qa.q: What could Reena try if the knee move does not work on a taller seat, and why?
qa.a: Reena could test a new way, like using a low stool or asking Charu, because a move that worked on one sofa might not fit another height.

qa.q: How does Charu see Reena's method?
qa.a: Charu sees Reena improving with practice, which is why Charu counts quietly and lets the climbing continue.

grounding: A toddler starts each sofa climb with a knee on the cushion edge, having found that it helped, and gets steadily faster.

passage: Oskar dashed at the sofa and scrambled up the tall armrest, feet kicking, grinning. Halfway up a foot slid on the smooth cloth and Oskar dropped backward. Oma Clara, standing close, caught Oskar under the arms. The grin vanished, then a wail came. Clara sat down with Oskar on her lap, waited for the crying to ease, and patted the low seat cushion. "This way?"

qa.q: Who caught Oskar when the foot slid?
qa.a: Oma Clara caught Oskar under the arms.

qa.q: What was Oskar feeling at the start of the climb?
qa.a: Oskar was excited and eager, shown by the dash, the kicking feet and the grin.

qa.q: What could Oskar try instead of the tall armrest, and why?
qa.a: Oskar could use the low seat cushion with a knee up first, because it is closer to the floor and safer than a slippery armrest.

qa.q: How does Oma Clara see Oskar's dash at the armrest?
qa.a: Clara sees a risk; she stays close enough to catch Oskar and afterwards shows the safer seat without scolding.

grounding: A toddler scrambles at the tall armrest instead of the seat, slips and is caught by a grandparent because eagerness outran a check on safety.

passage: Raghav slid off the sofa edge, sat down with a bump and cried. Still crying, Raghav jumped at the very same spot, chest first, and slid off again. Again, the same jump, the same slide, louder cries. Nazia, Raghav's mother, put a cushion on the floor and crouched close, then held out her arms: "Come, let's rest a moment." Raghav took a long, hiccuping breath.

qa.q: How did Raghav try the sofa again after the bump?
qa.a: Raghav jumped at the very same spot, chest first.

qa.q: What was Raghav feeling while jumping the same way and crying louder?
qa.a: Raghav was frustrated and upset, and the growing cries show the feeling running ahead of any new plan.

qa.q: What could Raghav try after resting, and why?
qa.a: Raghav could try a different move, like a knee on the cushion edge, because repeating the same jump gives the same slide.

qa.q: How does Nazia see the repeated jumps?
qa.a: Nazia sees the same failed jump again and again, so she makes the floor softer, stays close and offers a rest so Raghav can stop and think.

grounding: After slipping, a toddler cries but jumps at the same spot the same way, so each attempt fails as before.
